leads.summary: A pill:false widget still gets text chosen for the pill, not the wallpaper underneath it
leads.consequence: On a transparent bar, with pills enabled and an opaque pale [bar] pill over a dark wallpaper, a widget configured with {"pill":false} draws no pill but still receives the single barForeground selected for that pale pill. ActiveWindow.qml:37 uses that shared color. A synthetic black-wallpaper/white-text/light-pill example picks #101010 at 1.104:1 contrast over the bare black background where white text would be 21:1. This can render an explicitly unpilled widget unreadable; next appearance/toggle keeps the wrong color until pills are disabled or colors changed.
leads.triage: dropped; pill:false widget using the pill text colour is documented in shell/plugins/bar/README.md:76; unchanged since 97118bab.

leads.summary: The absent-shell fallback toggles raw JSON rather than the effective theme-default bar state
leads.consequence: If shell.json omits bar.floating and a theme has [bar] margin=10, the bar already floats, yet `omarchy bar floating toggle` while the shell is absent writes true and reports success, leaving it floating. If the theme sets [bar] pills="widget" with no JSON override, `pills toggle` writes section rather than turning pills off. The writes also make the values explicit, masking later theme changes; a repeat finally turns them off, rather than serving as a toggle on the first invocation. Applies also to the successful no-bar response. The documentation says a running bar uses effective state, but fallback should either resolve the theme or disclose/fail on indeterminate theme defaults.
leads.triage: dropped; Absent-shell fallback flips raw shell.json; documented behaviour (plugins.md, PR description) and the fallback the earlier review proposed.

leads.summary: An old running shell's Function not found is treated as an absent shell and produces a false-success toggle
leads.consequence: During a mixed-version upgrade the CLI can call a shell process that has no toggleBarPills/toggleBarFloating method. Quickshell reports Function not found (bin/omarchy-shell fails nonzero), yet toggle_in_shell classifies this as no bar and falls back to writing shell.json, then prints `Bar ... toggled` and exits 0. The old running bar has no code to render those options, so the user sees no change until restart; another toggle against that process can flip the file back. Unlike a missing shell, this response establishes that the targeted IPC method is unavailable on a live instance. Consider reporting an upgrade-needed failure, or use an explicitly supported compatibility path with clear deferred semantics.
leads.triage: dropped; Function not found. from an older shell is classified as no shell by design (code comment); Opus matrix corroborates the classification; version-skew-only.

leads.summary: Open PR #13569 implements an incompatible floating bar under the same bar.floating and cmd_floating identifiers
leads.consequence: #13569 is not an ancestor (compare status diverged) and has a separate floating windowExtent/barSurface/mask strategy plus its own cmd_floating. Merging its bin/omarchy-bar with this PR's head using #13569's real merge-base 97a9fce yields five conflict regions, including the cmd_floating toggle path: this PR asks a live bar over IPC, #13569 always edits JSON. Choosing either side blindly loses the other's semantics; coordinate the feature branches or close/supersede one before landing both. The other PR's own GitHub mergeable state was MERGEABLE when checked, which is not proof it merges with this PR.
leads.triage: verified_published; #13569 (other author, open) adds bar.floating and omarchy bar floating with a one-gaps_out inset; verified by coordinator gh api (coord/pr13569.diff) and Opus self-check (opus/related/). Noted in Details.

leads.summary: Open PR #13570 collides with pill grouping on the same layout group setting
leads.consequence: #13570 independently uses a layout entry's `group` to pad joined widgets and paint soft ovals; this PR uses the same group key to split pill runs and treats changing it as structural (returns null from inlineSettingsDelta). Both are distinct non-stacked PR heads. A three-way merge against #13570's real merge-base 97a9fce produces conflicts in both Bar.qml and BarModel.js (14 and 1 regions). Merely retaining both without resolving semantics paints two grouping backgrounds and makes #13570's live `omarchy bar set <id> group` rebuild the bar instead of its promised in-place regroup. Coordinate before merging rather than choosing conflicting chunks automatically.
leads.triage: verified_published; #13570 uses layout group key for ovals; this PR uses group change to split pill runs. Verified (coord/pr13570.diff). Noted in Details.

leads.summary: New bar toggle tests pass when the shared config writer is removed
leads.consequence: A plausible mutant deleting `config.bar[key] = value` inside Bar.qml:setBarOption keeps both QML toggle handlers and IPC routes but neither right-click nor running-shell CLI toggle can persist pills/floating. All 246 bar-test.sh lines still pass under LC_ALL=C. config-test.sh fakes the entire omarchy-shell process with an unconditional `ok`, and its running-shell checks only assert that the request was sent and shell.json stayed unchanged by the stub. Add a test that exercises setBarOption with a fake mutator and checks the resulting fields, and a negative case for the no-op writer. This is a test-strength lead below behavioral bugs.
leads.triage: dropped; Generic test-strength point (regex-based bar-test); no demonstrated user-facing benefit beyond existing coverage; not published.
